role: Head of the Criminal Investigation Division (CID)
businessContext: Runs a CID of 40 detectives handling roughly 600 open cases at any time, ranging from theft to homicide. Case files are currently a mix of paper folders, shared spreadsheets, and emailed PDFs, making it hard to track evidence, link related cases, or produce records for court.
communicationStyle: Formal and guarded, speaks in procedural and law-enforcement terminology, reluctant to disclose sensitive operational details until the developer earns trust.
goals: Cut down the hours detectives spend on paperwork
Close cases faster by spotting connections between them
Pass internal and external compliance audits without scrambling
constraints: Fixed annual IT budget already approved, no room for scope creep
Small internal IT staff with no dedicated developers
nonNegotiables: Every access to a case file must be logged and traceable to a specific officer
Evidence handling must produce a chain of custody that holds up in court
Victim and informant details must be restricted on a strict need-to-know basis
ambiguityPoints: Whether the system must integrate with the state/national crime database is still under internal review
Undecided whether patrol officers get read access or only detectives
Retention period for closed and cold case records has not been finalized
